- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to sentiment peak.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (sentiment < 0.3) — add 3–7% to forecast to compensate for mean reversion bias.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes — cap forecast 1–3 days post-spike at 5–10% below peak.
- Lagged mean reversion: if 3–5 day moving average of history is below forecast, adjust downward by 1–3% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid overfitting to recent volatility — smooth forecast using 7-day rolling average of history if sentiment is neutral or declining.
- If sentiment is rising but price is falling, reduce forecast slope — sentiment momentum overrides price momentum in correction rules.
